title: Armenia, Azerbaijan and Russia sign ceasefire statement ending the 44-day war
body:
The trilateral statement was signed on 9 November 2020 by Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Russian President Vladimir Putin, who mediated. It took effect at 00:00 Moscow time on 10 November 2020 and ended the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War, which had begun on 27 September. Artsakh's president, Arayik Harutyunyan, also agreed to end hostilities. Both sides were to hold their current positions.

Under its nine points, Agdam District was to return to Azerbaijan by 20 November 2020, followed by Kalbajar, with the deadline later extended to 25 November, and Lachin by 1 December. About 2,000 Russian peacekeepers with armoured vehicles were to deploy along the contact line and the Lachin Corridor, a five-kilometre route that bypasses Shusha, for five years, renewable automatically unless either side gave notice six months before expiry. A peacekeeping centre would monitor compliance. Displaced persons would return under UNHCR supervision, prisoners and bodies would be exchanged, and economic and transport links would be unblocked, with Armenia guaranteeing a route between western Azerbaijan and Nakhchivan overseen by Russia's Border Guard Service.

Russian troops began entering the region on 10 November. Aliyev described the deal as Armenia's capitulation, while Pashinyan said it was not a victory. In Yerevan the announcement triggered violent protests, and a crowd stormed parliament and assaulted Speaker Ararat Mirzoyan. France, Russia, Turkey, the United Kingdom and the European Union were among those welcoming the end of hostilities.
